probe: Can indefinite deletion-safe identity non-reuse be compacted without a finite optional hosted-storage dependency while preserving exact duplicate safety? Compare exact sets, probabilistic filters, cryptographic commitments/accumulators, and structural monotone identity schemes.
tested_scope: Documentation-level and information-theoretic architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST state, public technical sources, and direct reasoning. No O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected authority, external effect, hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package service, paid/trial API/model, manual execution, scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff, or optional second leaf.

direct_proof.arbitrary_exact_set_lower_bound: For a universe of U possible identities with exactly n used identities, an exact membership representation that distinguishes every possible used set needs at least log2(C(U,n)) bits. Therefore exact indefinite non-reuse for arbitrary unbounded identities cannot remain bounded-space as n and/or U grow.
direct_proof.prefix_state_reduction: If the valid committed identity set is structurally restricted to the contiguous prefix {0,...,H}, only the high-water mark H is needed. The representation is O(log H) bits and membership is exact: id <= H is already committed/reserved; id = H+1 is the only next admissible identity.
direct_proof.structural_cost: The compact prefix representation is valid only when allocation/commit is serialized or atomically coupled, successful effects never leave permanent gaps, an uncommitted identity is never exposed as committed, retries reuse the same identity, and old generations cannot re-enter a closed namespace.

append_only_exact_identity_set.storage: grows with distinct identities; lower bounded by exact-set information content
append_only_exact_identity_set.deletion_replay: safe if reservations are never deleted
append_only_exact_identity_set.zero_optional_quota_fit: poor for indefinite operation because reservation state grows without bound
append_only_exact_identity_set.hidden_side_effect_coverage: only if identity reservation is atomically bound to the external effect or that effect is independently idempotent

fixed_size_bloom_filter.false_positive: nonzero and rises as inserts accumulate; NIST analyzes false-positive behavior
fixed_size_bloom_filter.false_negative: none for insertion-only operation under the normal Bloom-filter model
fixed_size_bloom_filter.duplicate_safety: conservative: duplicates are not admitted because false positives reject rather than admit
fixed_size_bloom_filter.deletion_replay: safe only without deletion; fixed capacity eventually saturates
fixed_size_bloom_filter.zero_optional_quota_fit: fails useful indefinite parity because false-positive probability tends toward rejection of fresh identities; resizing restores liveness by reintroducing storage growth

append_only_merkle_commitment.duplicate_safety: exact only when the underlying log/proof material is available
append_only_merkle_commitment.storage: root is constant-size but the append-only entries/proof source still grow; RFC 6962 uses inclusion and consistency proofs over an append-only Merkle log
append_only_merkle_commitment.deletion_replay: strong append-only integrity, but root alone cannot decide arbitrary non-membership without proof/source state
append_only_merkle_commitment.zero_optional_quota_fit: does not eliminate growing state by itself

universal_cryptographic_accumulator.false_positive: cryptographic soundness error under stated assumptions rather than ordinary data-structure FP
universal_cryptographic_accumulator.false_negative: not the main tradeoff; correctness depends on valid witnesses and accumulator state
universal_cryptographic_accumulator.storage: accumulator value and witnesses can be succinct, but witness generation/update requires maintained set/update state or a prover/manager; moving that responsibility outward is a residual dependency
universal_cryptographic_accumulator.deletion_replay: dynamic constructions exist but add cryptographic witness/update machinery
universal_cryptographic_accumulator.zero_optional_quota_fit: unproven for the scheduled-Chat-only path without an external prover or growing locally maintained state
universal_cryptographic_accumulator.hidden_side_effect_coverage: not solved by the accumulator alone

serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.duplicate_safety: exact within the strict contiguous-prefix/atomic-commit scope
serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.storage: O(log H) current reservation state; no per-identity tombstone set
serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.deletion_replay: old identities stay rejected forever by the high-water mark; no clock or tombstone TTL required
serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.zero_optional_quota_fit: best of compared candidates for additional duplicate-reservation state; it uses only a compact durable scalar and no optional hosted compute/storage service, while overall checkpoint transport capacity remains a separate system-level question
serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.integration_cost: low to medium because identity issuance semantics must be changed
serialized_prefix_high_water_mark.hidden_side_effect_coverage: requires atomic coupling of high-water advancement and effect completion, or independently idempotent side effects

semantic_conclusion: No bounded representation can exactly remember an arbitrary indefinitely growing set of used identities. Probabilistic filters can bound memory only by accepting false positives and eventual liveness collapse; Merkle roots and cryptographic accumulators compress commitments but do not remove the need for proof/set/update state. The best transversal compact pattern is therefore structural rather than probabilistic: constrain committed effect identities to a serialized contiguous prefix and persist only a high-water mark. This eliminates per-identity tombstones, retry-horizon clocks, and deletion retention for that exact scope. It is not universal: arbitrary or out-of-order identities, preallocated gaps, concurrent independent issuers, and hidden non-atomic side effects remain unresolved unless converted to the same serialized atomic effect stream or protected by independent idempotence.
